item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 132316
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Tue Oct 13 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Simon, located about 100 miles west of Cabo Corrientes, Mexico, and
on recently upgraded Tropical Storm Trudy, located several hundred
miles south-southeast of Acapulco, Mexico.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&
Public advisories on Tropical Storm Trudy are issued under WMO
header WTPZ31 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP1.
Forecast/advisories on Tropical Storm Trudy are issued under WMO
header WTPZ21 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP1.

$$
Forecaster Mahoney

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Public Advisory Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Tue Oct 13 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 132036
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Trudy Advisory Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
300 PM CST Tue Oct 13 2026
 
...TRUDY FORECAST TO RAPIDLY INTENSIFY TO A MAJOR HURRICANE OVER 
THE NEXT FEW DAYS...
...RESIDENTS OF SOUTHWESTERN AND WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO SHOULD MONITOR
TRUDY'S PROGRESS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...10.6N 96.5W
ABOUT 490 MI...790 KM SSE OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 780 MI...1255 KM SE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 320 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in southwestern and west-central Mexico should monitor
the progress of Trudy.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header 
WTPZ41 KNHC. 

At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Trudy was
located near latitude 10.6 North, longitude 96.4 West. Trudy is
moving toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h). A motion between
west-northwest and northwest should continue through Wednesday
night.  A turn toward the north-northwest and a decrease in forward
speed is expected on Thursday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 40 mph (65 km/h)
with higher gusts. Rapid intensification is forecast during the next
3 days, and the cyclone is expected to become a hurricane by
Wednesday night and a major hurricane by Friday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southern Mexico late this week.  These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Tue Oct 13 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 132037
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Trudy Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
300 PM CST Tue Oct 13 2026
 
Satellite images indicate that the tropical cyclone continues to
become better organized.  Both microwave and geostationary satellite
data indicate that the center is likely about 60 miles to the
east-northeast of the previous estimate, and based on recent data,
confidence in the initial position estimate is a little higher now.
The improving low-level center appears to be located near the
southwest edge of a recent burst of deep convection.  The latest
subjective Dvorak classification from TAFB is T2.5/35 kt, and a
recent AiDT intensity estimate from UW-CIMSS is also 35 kt.  An
ASCAT pass from 1452 UTC had a couple of believable 31-kt vectors
north of the center.  Given the low bias of the ASCAT instrument due
to its resolution, and based on the improving structure observed on
satellite imagery since that time with increased banded convection
near the low-level center, the depression is upgraded to Tropical
Storm Trudy with 35-kt winds.
 
The initial motion estimate for Trudy is northwestward, or 320/7 kt.
A west-northwestward to northwestward motion is expected over the
next 36 hours while a mid-level ridge persists over the northwestern
Gulf of America.  Thereafter, a turn more toward the north-northwest
is likely as the ridge weakens.  A decrease in forward speed is also
expected by day 2 as the cyclone gets caught in weaker steering
currents in between the weak ridge to its north and Hurricane Simon
to its northwest.  Spread in the track forecast is larger than
normal from day 3 to 5, and some of this uncertainty is likely also
due to uncertainty in Simon's track and strength.  A cold front
moving southward from Texas into Mexico toward the end of the
forecast period could help draw Simon closer to the coastline of
Mexico, if the front is potent enough.  Regardless, Trudy could
potentially be very close to the coast of Mexico as a hurricane over
the weekend.  The NHC forecast has been pushed to the right (east)
of the previous forecast due to the farther east initial position
and a net eastward shift in the model guidance during the first 3
days of the forecast.  At days 4 and 5, the new NHC forecast is only
slightly east of the previous NHC forecast, which would bring Trudy
closer to the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico.  The
new NHC forecast is very close to the latest Google DeepMind
Ensemble Mean.  Confidence in the track forecast remains low,
especially from hour 72 to 120.
 
The cyclone is forecast to traverse extremely favorable oceanic and
atmospheric conditions for the next 4 days or so.  The NHC intensity
forecast shows steady strengthening over the next 12 hours as the
cyclone works to develop a convective core.  After that time, rapid
intensification is forecast during the 12 to 60 h time window. Some
of the SHIPS rapid intensification guidance shows a fairly high
chance of rapid intensification over the next few days. The NHC
intensity forecast shows 80 knots of strengthening over the next 72
h, and is in excellent agreement with the latest HCCA and GDMI.  90
percent of the Google DeepMind Ensemble Members are forecasting
Trudy to become a major hurricane.  The NHC intensity forecast is
similar to the previous one, and it's possible that Trudy could get
stronger in between the day 3 and 4 points, when the cyclone is
likely to peak in intensity.  Beyond day 4, the possibility of
increasing vertical wind shear and land interaction could induce
some weakening, and most of the guidance shows the system losing
some strength after day 4.  Confidence in the intensity forecast is
above average.  We are fairly confident it will become a strong
hurricane due to the favorable environmental conditions and model
guidance.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Trudy is forecast to be a major hurricane as it approaches the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico late this week and
into the weekend. There is an increasing risk of wind, rain, and
storm surge impacts, but it is too soon to determine the exact
location or magnitude of these impacts.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  13/2100Z 10.6N  96.5W   35 KT  40 MPH
 12H  14/0600Z 11.3N  97.5W   45 KT  50 MPH
 24H  14/1800Z 12.0N  99.0W   60 KT  70 MPH
 36H  15/0600Z 12.7N 100.1W   75 KT  85 MPH

120H  18/1800Z 19.1N 105.2W  100 KT 115 MPH
 
$$

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 26a
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM MST Tue Oct 13 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 132334
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Intermediate Advisory Number 26A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
500 PM MST Tue Oct 13 2026
 
...SMALL SIMON NEARLY STATIONARY OFF THE COAST OF WEST-CENTRAL 
MEXICO...
...INTERESTS THERE AND BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR SHOULD CONTINUE TO 
MONITOR THE HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM MST...0000 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.2N 107.4W
ABOUT 110 MI...180 KM W OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 110 MI...180 KM SW OF LAS ISLAS MARIAS MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 260 DEGREES AT 2 MPH...4 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...977 MB...28.85 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests in west-central Mexico and in Baja California Sur should 
continue to monitor as new watches and warnings may be issued over 
the next day or two.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM MST (0000 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located 
near latitude 20.2 North, longitude 107.4 West. Simon is drifting 
toward the west near 2 mph (4 km/h). The hurricane is forecast to 
move very slowly and erratically over the next couple of days. An 
eventual turn to the north or north-northwest is forecast to occur 
late this week.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher
gusts. Some slight strengthening is possible over the next day or 
so, and Simon is forecast to remain a hurricane through Thursday. 
Gradual weakening is forecast thereafter.
 
Simon is a very small hurricane. Hurricane-force winds extend 
outward up to 10 miles (20 km) from the center and 
tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 977 mb (28.85 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are possible within the hurricane watch
area for Las Islas Marias on Wednesday or Thursday.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 1 to 2
inches with isolated maximum amounts of 3 inches over portions of
the states of Baja California Sur, Nayarit, and Sinaloa by Friday.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 26
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Tue Oct 13 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 132059
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  26
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 PM MST Tue Oct 13 2026
 
Simon's structure this afternoon has been more or less steady state 
as its small eye continues to be discernible on both visible and 
infrared images. However, the surrounding eyewall cloud top 
temperatures have warmed a bit this afternoon, though it is unclear 
if this is a diurnal fluctuation or evidence of some cooler ocean 
upwelling given its slow motion. The most recent high-resolution 
microwave image was an WSFM pass at 1338 UTC, which showed a nearly 
closed eyewall and improvement from earlier imagery. The eye 
signature can also be picked up on the edge of the Cabo San 
Lucas, Mexico radar. The D-MINT mean estimate associated with the 
WSFM pass was 79 kt, and the initial intensity is held at 80 kt 
this advisory, on the higher end of the intensity estimates. A 
partial Metop-B scatterometer pass was useful to indicate how 
compact Simon's wind field has become, with 34-kt winds now only 
extend out an estimated 30 n mi.
 
The initial motion now appears to be a south of due west drift, or 
260 degrees at 2 kt. Compared to this morning, the forecast track 
reasoning has not changed a ton. The small hurricane is currently 
just on the south side of a saddle point, or col, in the steering 
flow. Simon's future track is very sensitive to which side of this 
point the hurricane is located, with light steering currents 
prevailing leading to slow motion. In the latest round of guidance, 
all of the hurricane-regional models show a more substantial 
southward track this afternoon while Simon remains in very light 
deep-layer southerly steering. While the ECMWF forecast is further 
north, it was initialized almost a full degree further north of 
where Simon was located at 12 UTC, placing it over or just on the 
north side of the saddle point. The Google Deepmind ensembles, which 
often favors this initialization, jump north in the short term, 
which appears unrealistic. Thus, the latest NHC track forecast is 
going to place a little more weight on the hurricane-regional model 
tracks which had a better initialization, showing a little more 
southward motion over the next 24-36 h, albeit as a snail's pace. 
This track still shows a small cyclonic loop and is south of the 
previous track forecast. After 48 h, the large-scale synoptic 
pattern finally begins to change, where a deep-layer cutoff low digs 
into southern California. This pattern will induce more southerly 
environmental flow over Simon, and should dislodge it from this very 
stagnant steering pattern assuming it doesn't move as far south as 
the HAFS-A/B track aids. The NHC track forecast still shows Simon 
gaining latitude and turning more north-northwest in 60-72 h and 
lies closest to the HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA) track. 
This could bring Simon closer to the coast of Baja California Sur as 
it moves up the Gulf of California. However, there remains a wide 
variety of track solutions that could verify, from well south of 
Baja California northward to mainland Mexico over the next 5 days.
 
Simon has maintained a relatively healthy appearance today with a 
well-organized inner core. As stressed earlier, very small 
hurricanes like Simon are known to be sensitive to small changes in 
their environmental conditions that could result in rapid changes in 
intensity, either up or down. Environmental conditions are 
favorable, with shear over Simon expected to remain low for the next 
48 h with sea-surface temperatures (SSTs) in the 28-30 C range. 
Assuming Simon does not completely stall and upwell cooler ocean 
waters, some intensification could occur. With that said, there is 
an extreme range of intensity solutions over the next 48 h, from 
intensifying into a Category 4 hurricane (HAFS-A) to weakening to a 
tropical storm (HMON). Given the current structure, the latest NHC 
intensity forecast now shows some intensification, but remains well 
under the latest HAFS-A forecast and is closest to the ECMWF LGEM 
guidance. After 48 h, southwesterly vertical wind shear is forecast 
to increase rather quickly, and the small sensitive Simon is 
forecast to weaken even as it moves over warmer SSTs when it tracks 
northward. This latest forecast is initially on the high side of the 
guidance, but falls back to the middle of the guidance envelope 
after 
72 h.
 
It is worth stressing that this remains a very low confidence
forecast for both track and intensity, and interests in west-central
Mexico and Baja California Sur should continue to closely monitor
the latest updates. While mainland Tropical Storm and Hurricane
watches have been discontinued, new watches and warnings could be
required over the next day or two as Simon's ultimate forecast comes
into better focus.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Simon could approach Las Islas Marias on Wednesday and the coast
of western Mexico later this week at or near hurricane strength, and
a Hurricane Watch is in effect for a portion of these areas.
Interests in west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur should
continue to closely monitor the latest updates to Simon's forecast.
Changes to watches and warnings could be required over the next day 
or two based on the latest forecast trends.
 
2. Large swells will affect portions of the southwestern and
west-central coasts of Mexico over the next several days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions.
